name: Breaking the Wall
description: Monocarp plays "Rage of Empires II: Definitive Edition" — a strategic computer game. Right now he's planning to attack his opponent in the game, but Monocarp's forces cannot enter the opponent's territory since the opponent has built a wall. The wall consists of $$$n$$$ sections, aligned in a row. The $$$i$$$-th section initially has durability $$$a_i$$$. If durability of some section becomes $$$0$$$ or less, this section is considered broken. To attack the opponent, Monocarp needs to break at least two sections of the wall (any two sections: possibly adjacent, possibly not). To do this, he plans to use an onager — a special siege weapon. The onager can be used to shoot any section of the wall; the shot deals $$$2$$$ damage to the target section and $$$1$$$ damage to adjacent sections. In other words, if the onager shoots at the section $$$x$$$, then the durability of the section $$$x$$$ decreases by $$$2$$$, and the durability of the sections $$$x - 1$$$ and $$$x + 1$$$ (if they exist) decreases by $$$1$$$ each. Monocarp can shoot at any sections any number of times, he can even shoot at broken sections . Monocarp wants to calculate the minimum number of onager shots needed to break at least two sections. Help him!
input_specification: The first line contains one integer $$$n$$$ ($$$2 \le n \le 2 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of sections. The second line contains the sequence of integers $$$a_1, a_2, \dots, a_n$$$ ($$$1 \le a_i \le 10^6$$$), where $$$a_i$$$ is the initial durability of the $$$i$$$-th section.
output_specification: Print one integer — the minimum number of onager shots needed to break at least two sections of the wall.
approach_summary: Verify predicate monotonicity: P(x) is true for x ≤ K and false otherwise. Binary search over the answer domain to find the boundary in O(log(Range) × Verify_Time).

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1674E — Breaking the Wall [33. Binary Search]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary search on the monotonic answer domain.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: The predicate function $P(x)$ ('Is answer $\le x$ feasible?') is monotonic: if $P(x)$ is true for some value, it remains true for all larger values (or vice versa). This allows binary division of the answer search space $[\text{low}, \text{high}]$ in $O(\log(\text{Range}))$.
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N \log(\text{Range}))$
  The binary search divides the search interval by 2 at each iteration, requiring $\log_2(\text{Range})$ steps. In each step, the feasibility check `check(mid)` scans the array in $\mathcal{O}(N)$ time.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(1)$ auxiliary space
  The algorithm operates directly over the input array without allocating extra auxiliary memory.
